sentences.text: Picture this. You are running two AI coding helpers on the same project.
They are fast. But they cannot see each other.
Helper A changes a function. It now needs one more input: the tenant.
Helper B is working in another file. It still calls the function the old way.
Nobody tells anybody. And the test breaks.
The next day, a new helper starts. It knows nothing.
Yesterday you said: never use sqlite, the server is read-only. The new helper adds sqlite anyway.
This is MeshAgents.
A shared memory for AI coding helpers.
It runs quietly as a Claude Code plugin. You type nothing.
Same job, same two helpers. Without it on the left. With MeshAgents on the right.
Helper A's edit is written into the graph.
Before B edits, it gets a warning. And A is told which callers may break.
B adjusts its call. The tests pass.
The next day, the new helper is briefed on the rule. So it uses a JSON file instead.
You can watch it all on a live board.
And see exactly what the next helper is told: about 370 tokens.
Under the hood it is a graph, built on FalkorDB.
Every warning is a question asked of the graph. Who is working on this file?
What breaks if I change this function?
What was this note based on? If a note is wrong, you see everything built on it.
One query claims a task safely. Taking back a wrong note takes about 3 milliseconds. And git history shows which files change together.
Does it work? In 180 runs, clean results went from 53 percent to 80.
A new session finishing its job: 45 percent with no memory, 92 with a notes file, and 95 with MeshAgents.
One rule hidden among 20 others: found 10 times out of 10.
Each clean result costs 29 percent less. A single run costs about the same.
And on a second, stronger model: 33 percent to 83.
Now, the honest part.
The tests are built to make helpers collide, so real projects will see fewer clashes.
A notes file does about as well on memory, but someone has to keep it up.
And one test, two helpers adding the same stock reservation, is still not fixed.
Try it. Clone the repo, run meshagents doctor, and start Claude Code with the plugin.
MeshAgents. A shared memory for AI coding helpers. Built on FalkorDB.
